title: Inferring Experimental Objectives in Microscopy Experiments from Decision Traces
abstract: arXiv:2611.29814v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Modern microscopes can acquire, analyze and act on data far faster than human operators can decide what to measure next. Exploiting this speed in automated experiments requires the instrument to follow the scientific logic of the operator, and one way to encode that logic is through reward functions that become part of the operation process. Here we explore whether such reward functions can be learned from the decision histories of microscope operators. We propose multiple frameworks in which recorded choices among alternative measurement locations serve as comparative evidence about the operator's preferences, and we compare several algorithms for reconstructing the reward including interpretable linear models built on physically meaningful image descriptors, nonlinear functions of the same descriptors, an unsupervised image representation followed by preference modeling, and a preference trained deep kernel inspired model. The result

translated_title: 从决策轨迹推断显微实验中的实验目标
translated_abstract: 现代显微镜获取、分析并处理数据的速度远远超过人类操作员决定下一步测量内容的速度。要在自动化实验中充分利用这种速度，需要仪器遵循操作员的科学逻辑，而编码这种逻辑的一种方式是通过成为操作过程一部分的奖励函数。本文探讨了是否可以从显微镜操作员的决策历史中学习这种奖励函数。我们提出了多种框架，将操作员在不同候选测量位置之间做出的记录选择作为关于其偏好的比较证据，并比较了多种重建奖励函数的算法，包括基于具有物理意义的图像描述符构建的可解释线性模型、基于相同描述符的非线性函数、无监督图像表示结合偏好建模，以及一种受深度核启发、经偏好训练的模型。结果表明……
tldr: 本文提出从显微镜操作员的决策历史中学习奖励函数以推断其实验目标，并比较了多种从操作员对测量位置的选择偏好中重建奖励函数的算法框架。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes inferring experimental objectives by learning reward functions from microscope operators' decision histories, comparing multiple algorithms that reconstruct operator preferences from recorded choices among alternative measurement locations.
